primaryParams.label: Requests/Second
primaryParams.costDriver: Maximum requests per second before degradation.
primaryParams.notes: Maximum requests per second this API can handle before request throttling kicks in. Set this to match your expected peak traffic.

primaryParams.label: Base Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Processing delay per request.
primaryParams.notes: Processing delay added by this API layer before forwarding to backend. Affects simulation accuracy for latency-sensitive architectures.

primaryParams.label: Integration Timeout (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Maximum wait time for backend response before failing.
primaryParams.notes: How long the API waits for a backend response before returning a 504 Gateway Timeout. Match this to your downstream service SLA.

costParams.label: API Type
costParams.notes: Selects the API Gateway product tier. HTTP APIs are cheaper and faster; REST APIs offer advanced features like caching, request validation, and usage plans.

costParams.label: Cache Capacity (GB)
costParams.notes: Dedicated in-memory cache for REST API responses. Reduces backend calls for repeated identical requests, improving latency and cutting downstream costs.

costParams.label: Connection Minutes (M/mo)
costParams.costDriver: WebSocket APIs bill for total connection time at $0.25 per million connection minutes, in addition to per-message charges.
costParams.notes: Total minutes all clients stay connected per month, in millions. Example: 1,000 always-on connections ≈ 43.8M minutes/month. Only applies to WebSocket APIs.

components.name: API Request Cost
components.note: HTTP=$1.00/M, REST=$3.50/M, WebSocket=$1.00/M messages + $0.25/M connection minutes

components.name: Data Transfer Out
components.note: First 100 GB/mo free across all AWS services

components.name: Cache Infrastructure
components.note: Only applies to REST APIs with caching enabled

freeTier.description: 1M REST + 1M HTTP + 1M WebSocket messages free/month for 12 months

primaryParams.label: Requests/Second
primaryParams.costDriver: Maximum requests per second before degradation. DNS queries are billed based on this volume.
primaryParams.notes: Estimated DNS queries per second your zone receives. Determines the DNS query cost tier.

primaryParams.label: Base Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: DNS resolution time added before reaching origin.
primaryParams.notes: Simulated DNS resolution latency for routing simulation purposes.

costParams.label: Hosted Zones
costParams.costDriver: First 25 zones at $0.50/mo, additional at $0.10/mo
costParams.notes: The number of DNS hosted zones you manage. Each zone covers a domain or subdomain (e.g. example.com). AWS charges per zone per month.

components.name: Hosted Zone Cost
components.note: First 25 zones at $0.50/mo, additional at $0.10/mo

components.name: DNS Query Cost
components.note: First 1B queries at $0.40/M, above 1B at $0.20/M

freeTier.description: Alias queries to AWS resources are free.

primaryParams.label: Requests/Second
primaryParams.costDriver: Billed per request: RPS × 2.628 = millions of requests/month. Drives the CloudFront Requests cost line (rate set by the Users node's region).

primaryParams.label: Base Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Edge-to-origin delay per request.

primaryParams.label: Cache Hit Ratio (%)
primaryParams.costDriver: Higher cache hit = less origin load & lower origin transfer cost.

costParams.label: Traffic Region
costParams.costDriver: Sets the CloudFront edge price class for both data transfer and requests. Locked to the Users node's Request Region — change it there.
costParams.notes: Locked to the Users node's Request Region. CloudFront bills by edge geography, so this region determines the per-GB transfer and per-request rates.

costParams.label: Data Transfer Out (GB)
costParams.notes: Estimated gigabytes of content delivered to end users monthly. Main cost driver for CloudFront-heavy architectures (video, large assets). Request count is derived from Requests/Second; the edge price class follows the Users node's Request Region.

costParams.label: Enable WAF
costParams.notes: Enables AWS WAF on this distribution to block malicious traffic. Adds a WAF Web ACL base charge plus per-request inspection fee.

components.name: Request Cost
components.note: HTTP=$0.75/M, HTTPS=$1.00/M (US/EU)

components.name: Origin Shield
components.note: Additional per-request charge on top of standard pricing

components.name: Invalidation Cost
components.note: First 1,000 paths/mo free

freeTier.description: Always free: 1 TB transfer out + 10M requests/mo.

primaryParams.label: Requests/Second
primaryParams.costDriver: RPS × 2,628,000 sec/mo = monthly invocations billed. Directly drives request and GB-second costs.
primaryParams.notes: Maximum requests per second this function handles. Combined with concurrency and duration to determine actual throughput cap. Also used to compute monthly invocation count for billing.

primaryParams.label: Avg Execution Time (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Directly multiplied with memory to determine GB-second billing.
primaryParams.notes: Average function execution time in milliseconds. Drives both end-to-end latency simulation and GB-second cost calculation.

primaryParams.label: Reserved Concurrency
primaryParams.costDriver: Hard cap on simultaneous executions — throttles requests beyond this limit.
primaryParams.notes: Maximum simultaneous in-flight executions. Acts as a hard ceiling: effective max RPS = concurrency ÷ (executionTime/1000). Throttled requests return 429 TooManyRequests.

costParams.label: Architecture
costParams.notes: CPU instruction set. ARM/Graviton2 is ~20% cheaper and often faster for compute-bound workloads.

costParams.label: Memory (MB)
costParams.notes: RAM per invocation. Lambda bills GB-seconds = (memoryMB/1024) × (durationMs/1000). Higher memory also allocates proportionally more CPU.

costParams.label: Avg Duration per Invocation (ms)
costParams.notes: Average function execution time billed per invocation. This is the core cost multiplier: Cost = invocations × (duration/1000) × (memory/1024) × rate/GB-sec. Lambda bills in 1ms increments.

costParams.label: Ephemeral Storage (MB)
costParams.notes: Temporary /tmp storage per invocation. First 512 MB is free; storage above 512 MB is billed per GB-second of execution.

costParams.label: Provisioned Concurrency
costParams.notes: Pre-warmed execution environments that eliminate cold starts. Billed 24/7 regardless of invocations. Essential for latency-sensitive functions.

components.name: Request Cost
components.note: Monthly invocations derived from RPS × 2,628,000 sec/mo. First 1M requests/mo always free.

components.name: Compute Cost (GB-seconds)
components.note: gbSeconds = (throughput × 2,628,000) × (durationMs/1000) × (memoryMB/1024). x86=$0.0000166667/GB-sec, ARM=$0.0000133334/GB-sec. First 400K GB-sec/mo free.

components.name: Provisioned Concurrency
components.note: Billed 24/7 even when idle. No free tier.

components.name: Ephemeral Storage
components.note: Only charged for storage above the included 512 MB

freeTier.description: Always free: 1M requests + 400K GB-seconds/mo.

primaryParams.label: Requests/Second
primaryParams.costDriver: Maximum requests per second before degradation.

primaryParams.label: Base Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Processing delay per request.

primaryParams.label: CPU Baseline (%)
primaryParams.costDriver: Steady-state CPU usage. Higher means less burst room.

primaryParams.label: Connection Limit
primaryParams.costDriver: Maximum concurrent TCP connections.

costParams.label: Instance Family
costParams.notes: Defines the hardware profile: t3=burstable/cheap, m5=general purpose, c5=compute-optimized, r5=memory-optimized. Choose based on workload characteristics.

costParams.label: Instance Size
costParams.notes: Scales vCPU and RAM within the chosen family. Larger sizes cost proportionally more. Match to your actual CPU/memory requirements.

costParams.label: Instance Count
costParams.notes: Number of EC2 instances running in parallel. Each instance is billed independently at the hourly rate.

costParams.label: Purchase Option
costParams.notes: Pricing model: On-Demand has no commitment, Reserved gives 40-60% discount with 1-3 year commitment, Spot can save 70%+ but instances can be interrupted.

costParams.label: EBS Volume Type
costParams.notes: EBS volume type attached to each instance. gp3 is the best default (cheaper than gp2 with better baseline performance). io2 for IOPS-intensive databases.

costParams.label: EBS Size per Node (GB)
costParams.notes: Root EBS volume size in GB per instance. Billed monthly at the per-GB rate for the selected volume type.

costParams.label: Data Transfer Out (GB)
costParams.notes: Data sent from EC2 to the internet monthly. First 100 GB/mo free. Use CloudFront or VPC endpoints to reduce these charges.

costParams.label: Operating System
costParams.costDriver: Windows includes the license in the hourly rate — roughly 1.45× the Linux price for general-purpose families.
costParams.notes: Instance operating system. Windows pricing bundles the OS license, which raises the hourly rate substantially.

components.note: On-Demand = no discount, Spot up to 90% off, Reserved up to 72% off

components.note: gp3=$0.08/GB, io1/io2=$0.125/GB per month

primaryParams.label: Requests/Second
primaryParams.costDriver: Maximum requests per second before degradation.

primaryParams.label: Base Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Object read/write response time.

costParams.label: Storage Class
costParams.notes: Determines retrieval speed, availability SLA, and cost tier. Standard is instant-access; SIA and Glacier trade retrieval time for lower storage costs.

costParams.label: Storage Amount (GB)
costParams.notes: Total data stored in S3 each month. This is the dominant cost driver for storage-heavy use cases.

costParams.label: PUT/COPY/POST (Millions)
costParams.notes: Millions of write/upload operations (PUT, COPY, POST) per month. Write operations cost more than reads, especially in Glacier tiers.

costParams.label: GET/SELECT (Millions)
costParams.notes: Millions of read/download operations (GET, SELECT) per month. GET costs are lower than PUT but can add up at scale.

costParams.label: Data Transfer Out (GB)
costParams.notes: Data downloaded from S3 to the internet monthly. Use CloudFront in front of S3 to shift costs to cheaper CDN transfer rates.

components.name: Storage Cost
components.note: Standard=$0.023/GB, IA=$0.0125/GB, Glacier Deep=$0.00099/GB

components.name: Data Transfer Out
components.note: First 100 GB/mo free across all AWS services

freeTier.description: 12 months: 5 GB storage, 2K PUT, 20K GET, 100 GB transfer/mo.

primaryParams.label: Requests/Second
primaryParams.costDriver: RPS drives the New Connections LCU dimension (RPS × newConnectionsPercent ÷ 25). Higher RPS = more LCUs billed.
primaryParams.notes: Maximum requests per second this load balancer routes. Used as the baseline for LCU dimension calculations.

primaryParams.label: Base Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Processing delay.
primaryParams.notes: Processing overhead added by the load balancer. Helps simulate realistic end-to-end request latency.

costParams.label: Load Balancer Type
costParams.costDriver: AWS offers ALB for HTTP/HTTPS, NLB for high-performance TCP/UDP, CLB for legacy setups, and GWLB for virtual appliances.
costParams.notes: The AWS load balancer product to use. ALB is recommended for HTTP/HTTPS microservices; NLB for ultra-low latency TCP; CLB for legacy apps; GWLB for inline security appliances.

costParams.label: Number of Load Balancers
costParams.costDriver: Number of load balancer instances provisioned to distribute incoming traffic. Billed hourly per load balancer.
costParams.notes: Number of load balancer instances. Each LB is billed independently at the hourly rate, then shares the LCU pool.

costParams.label: New Connections / sec (% of RPS)
costParams.costDriver: Percentage of RPS that results in a brand-new TCP/TLS handshake per second. For example, at 100 RPS with 10%, the LB handles 10 new connections/sec. AWS bills 1 LCU per 25 new conn/s (ALB), 800 new conn/s (NLB), or 600 new conn/s (GWLB).
costParams.notes: What percentage of your incoming RPS results in a brand-new TCP/TLS handshake. Stateless HTTP/2 reuses connections heavily (low %). Keep-alive disabled means higher new connection rates.

costParams.label: Active Connections (count)
costParams.costDriver: Total number of concurrent TCP connections that remain open at any moment. AWS bills 1 LCU per 3,000 active connections (ALB), 100,000 active flows (NLB), or 60,000 active flows (GWLB).
costParams.notes: Peak number of concurrent TCP connections open at any moment across all clients. Represents the size of your connection table, not request rate.

costParams.label: Average Package Size (KB)
costParams.costDriver: Dynamic request package size in KB, synced from the Client service parameters. Dictates the amount of processed data volume in LCU billing.
costParams.notes: Auto-synced from the Client (Users) node. Represents the average size of each request/response payload. Change this value on the Client node.

costParams.label: Rule Evaluations (M/mo)
costParams.costDriver: Rule evaluations per million/month. Charges apply for rule evaluations beyond the first 10 rules per listener.
costParams.notes: Number of routing rule evaluations per request (ALB only). AWS includes the first 10 rules free per listener. Applies to path-based and host-based routing rules.

primaryParams.label: Bandwidth (Mbps)
primaryParams.costDriver: Network throughput.
primaryParams.notes: Simulated bandwidth capacity of this VPC segment in the traffic flow model.

costParams.label: VPC Endpoints
costParams.notes: VPC Interface Endpoints that allow private connectivity to AWS services without traversing the internet. Each endpoint has an hourly charge plus data processing fee.

costParams.label: Endpoint Data (GB)
costParams.notes: Data processed through VPC Interface Endpoints monthly. Billed per GB in addition to the hourly endpoint charge.

costParams.label: Public IPv4 Addresses
costParams.costDriver: Every public IPv4 costs $0.005/hr (~$3.65/mo) since February 2024 — including those attached to EC2, NAT gateways, and load balancers.
costParams.notes: Count of public IPv4 addresses across this VPC (instance EIPs, NAT gateways, load balancer nodes). AWS has charged for all public IPv4s since Feb 2024.

primaryParams.label: Requests/Second
primaryParams.costDriver: Impacts data transfer.

primaryParams.label: Base Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Processing delay added per request in the simulation.
primaryParams.notes: NAT adds sub-millisecond forwarding overhead.

costParams.label: NAT Gateway Count
costParams.notes: Number of NAT Gateway instances. For high availability, deploy one per Availability Zone. Each NAT is billed hourly independently.

costParams.label: Data Processed (GB)
costParams.notes: Data processed through the NAT Gateway monthly. This is often the dominant NAT cost — use VPC endpoints for S3/DynamoDB to bypass NAT entirely.

costParams.label: Custom Metrics
costParams.notes: Number of custom CloudWatch metrics. AWS provides basic instance metrics free. Custom metrics (application-level) are charged per metric per month.

costParams.label: Logs Ingested (GB)
costParams.notes: Log data ingested into CloudWatch Logs monthly. This is often the largest CloudWatch cost driver — use log sampling or S3 export to reduce it.

costParams.label: Dashboards
costParams.notes: Number of custom CloudWatch dashboards. First 3 are free; each additional dashboard is $3/month.

costParams.label: Alarms
costParams.costDriver: Standard-resolution alarms bill $0.10/alarm/month.
costParams.notes: Metric alarms watching your stack. Every production architecture carries dozens — they add up quietly.

costParams.label: Logs Stored (GB)
costParams.costDriver: Stored (compressed) log data bills $0.03/GB/month — separate from the $0.50/GB ingestion charge.
costParams.notes: Cumulative retained log volume. Ingestion and storage are different line items on a real AWS bill.

components.name: Dashboards
components.note: 3 dashboards free

freeTier.description: 3 Dashboards free per month.

primaryParams.label: Requests/Second
primaryParams.costDriver: Requested operations per second. In provisioned mode the simulation caps this at what your RCU/WCU can serve.
primaryParams.notes: On-demand mode scales automatically. In provisioned mode the real ceiling is RCU/WCU — under-provisioning shows as throttling in the simulation.

primaryParams.label: Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: DynamoDB provides single-digit ms latency.

costParams.label: Capacity Mode
costParams.notes: On-Demand scales automatically (pay per request); Provisioned gives a steady capacity allocation at lower per-unit cost but requires capacity planning.

costParams.label: Table Class
costParams.notes: Standard is always-accessible; Infrequent Access (IA) is cheaper for tables read less than once per day.

costParams.label: Reads / Month (Millions)
costParams.notes: Millions of read requests per month (on-demand mode). One read request unit = up to 4KB strongly consistent read or 8KB eventually consistent.

costParams.label: Writes / Month (Millions)
costParams.notes: Millions of write requests per month (on-demand mode). Write request units are 5× more expensive than read units.

costParams.label: Provisioned WCU
costParams.notes: Provisioned Write Capacity Units (steady-state). 1 WCU = one write/sec for items up to 1KB. The highest DynamoDB cost driver.

costParams.label: Provisioned RCU
costParams.notes: Provisioned Read Capacity Units (steady-state). 1 RCU = one strongly consistent read/sec for items up to 4KB. Over-provision for predictable latency.

costParams.label: Storage Size (GB)
costParams.notes: Total data stored across all DynamoDB tables. First 25 GB/mo free globally.

costParams.label: Global Tables Enabled
costParams.notes: Multi-region active-active replication. Enables low-latency reads and writes worldwide, but multiplies WCU consumption by the number of replica regions.

costParams.label: Avg Item Size (KB)
costParams.costDriver: Capacity-unit math: a read consumes ceil(size/4KB) RCUs/RRUs, a write consumes ceil(size/1KB) WCUs/WRUs.
costParams.notes: Average item size. Items over 4 KB consume multiple read units; over 1 KB, multiple write units. The AWS calculator requires this — cost is wrong without it.

freeTier.description: 25 GB of storage free per month.

primaryParams.label: Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Query latency.

primaryParams.label: Max Connections
primaryParams.costDriver: Connection-pool ceiling — the classic RDS bottleneck. Effective max RPS ≈ connections ÷ query time.
primaryParams.notes: Instance-class connection limit (db.m5.large ≈ 800–1,000 for PostgreSQL). The simulation caps throughput at connections ÷ (latency in seconds).

costParams.label: Database Engine
costParams.notes: The database engine. PostgreSQL and MySQL are open-source and cheapest. Oracle and SQL Server require commercial licenses which add significant cost multipliers.

costParams.label: Instance Class
costParams.notes: The RDS instance type. Larger instances provide more vCPU, RAM, and network bandwidth. db.t3 is burstable; db.m5/r5 are steady-state workload instances.

costParams.label: Multi-AZ Deployment
costParams.notes: Synchronous standby replica in a different Availability Zone for automatic failover. Doubles the instance cost but eliminates single-AZ as a SPOF.

costParams.label: Instance Count (incl Replicas)
costParams.notes: Number of RDS instances (primary + read replicas). Each instance is billed at the full hourly rate.

costParams.label: Storage Type
costParams.notes: EBS storage type for the RDS database files. gp3 offers predictable IOPS at lower cost. io2 for high-throughput OLTP workloads.

costParams.label: Storage Size (GB)
costParams.notes: Allocated storage in GB. RDS storage is pre-provisioned and billed even if unused. You can always increase but not easily decrease.

costParams.label: Backup Storage (GB)
costParams.notes: Snapshot backup retention in GB. AWS provides free backup storage equal to your total database size. Additional backup storage beyond that is billed.

costParams.label: Read Replicas
costParams.costDriver: Each replica bills as a single-AZ instance of the same class and serves read traffic.
costParams.notes: Read replicas scale read throughput and bill like additional single-AZ instances. The simulation routes a share of reads to them.

primaryParams.label: Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Sub-millisecond latency.

primaryParams.label: Cache Hit Rate (%)
primaryParams.costDriver: Percent of reads served from memory. Higher hit rate boosts effective capacity and cuts latency.
primaryParams.notes: Share of requests answered from cache. Misses fall through to the database behind it — a low hit rate means your DB still takes most of the load.

costParams.label: Engine
costParams.notes: Cache engine. Redis adds replication and persistence; Memcached is simpler multi-threaded caching. Pricing is per node-hour and similar across engines.

costParams.label: Node Type
costParams.notes: Cache node size (CPU + RAM). Match to your working dataset: too small causes evictions and cache misses; too large wastes money.

costParams.label: Node Count
costParams.notes: Number of cache nodes in the cluster. More nodes give higher throughput and availability (cluster mode), each billed at the per-node hourly rate.

costParams.label: Data Tiering
costParams.notes: Extends usable cache capacity to SSD, allowing datasets larger than available RAM. Adds a cost premium but cheaper than equivalently-sized all-RAM nodes.

primaryParams.label: Latency (ms)
primaryParams.costDriver: Task latency.

costParams.label: Launch Type
costParams.notes: Execution model: Fargate removes server management (pay per task); EC2 mode uses your own instances (more control, potentially cheaper at scale).

costParams.label: Task Count
costParams.notes: Number of running task replicas. ECS scales tasks up/down automatically. Each task is billed by the vCPU and memory it reserves.

costParams.label: vCPU per Task
costParams.notes: vCPU units reserved per task. Fargate bills per vCPU-hour. More vCPU means faster processing but higher cost.

costParams.label: Memory per Task (GB)
costParams.notes: RAM reserved per task in GB. Fargate bills per GB-hour. Ensure your containers have enough headroom to avoid OOM kills.

costParams.label: Average Utilization (%)
costParams.notes: Average CPU utilization of running tasks. Used for simulation accuracy — doesn't affect billing directly but signals over/under-provisioning.

costParams.label: Monthly Runtime Hours
costParams.notes: Total hours per month tasks run. 730h = always-on; reduce for batch or off-hours workloads.

costParams.label: CPU Architecture
costParams.notes: Fargate CPU architecture. ARM (Graviton) is ~20% cheaper than x86 for the same vCPU/memory.

costParams.label: Ephemeral Storage (GB)
costParams.notes: Scratch disk per task beyond the free 20 GB. Billed at ~$0.000111/GB-hour on Fargate.

costParams.label: Spot Usage (%)
costParams.notes: Percentage of tasks running on Fargate Spot (interruptible, up to 70% cheaper). Only suitable for fault-tolerant, stateless tasks.

costParams.label: EC2 Instance Type
costParams.notes: EC2 instance type backing the ECS cluster (EC2 launch type only). Sets the per-hour compute rate.

costParams.label: EC2 Instance Count
costParams.notes: Number of EC2 container instances in the cluster. Each is billed at its full instance-hour rate.

costParams.label: Purchase Option
costParams.notes: EC2 pricing model: On-Demand (no commitment), Reserved (up to ~40% off for 1-3yr), or Spot (up to ~70% off, interruptible).

costParams.label: EBS Storage per Node (GB)
costParams.notes: EBS root volume size per EC2 container instance, billed per GB-month.

costParams.label: Data Transfer Out
costParams.notes: Outbound data to the internet per month. First 100 GB free, then ~$0.09/GB.

primaryParams.label: User Traffic (RPS)
primaryParams.costDriver: Source of simulation traffic. When Sync RPS is on, this value is pushed to every downstream service's Requests/Second.
primaryParams.notes: Steady-state traffic from your users. Hidden when Variable Traffic is on (replaced by Min/Max RPS range).

primaryParams.label: Sync RPS to all connected services
primaryParams.costDriver: When enabled, every downstream service's Requests/Second is forced to match the user traffic value. Disable to restore each service's original capacity.
primaryParams.notes: Propagates the user traffic value to the throughput of every service reachable from this client. Original capacities are restored on uncheck.

primaryParams.label: Variable Traffic
primaryParams.costDriver: When enabled, traffic randomly varies between Min/Max RPS each second during simulation. Cost shows the live per-sample monthly cost.
primaryParams.notes: Simulates real-world bursty traffic. During simulation a new RPS is sampled every second from the chosen range. Pre-run cost uses the midpoint of the range as an estimate.

primaryParams.label: Min RPS (Variable)
primaryParams.costDriver: Lower bound of randomly sampled traffic when Variable Traffic is on.

primaryParams.label: Max RPS (Variable)
primaryParams.costDriver: Upper bound of randomly sampled traffic when Variable Traffic is on.

primaryParams.label: Average Package Size (KB)
primaryParams.costDriver: Size of each request package sent from the client.

primaryParams.label: Request Region
primaryParams.costDriver: Select the region from where you are receiving maximum traffic
